newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel rejects broad interpretation of EMU targets.
newsitem.headline: Waigel rejects broad interpretation of EMU targets.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Wednesday rejected any broad interpretation of the fiscal criteria set out in the European Union's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"For me, the deficit criteria mean three percent and not 3.2 or 3.15," he said in a speech in Bonn.
Waigel added that the criteria for entry into a single European currency in 1999 must not be interpreted broadly as has been speculated on financial markets.
In order to participate in EMU in 1999, EU members in 1997 must show that budget deficits do not exceed three percent of gross domestic product and public debt cannot exceed 60 percent of GDP.
